chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the proofs (evidence) were made for the lineage and the inheritances. And in another report: And the legal punishments (Hudud).

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَاتُ: The proofs or evidence (plural of bayyinah)
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: Legal punishments or fixed penalties (singular: hadd)

ai.seo_question: What are the primary areas in Islamic law where formal proofs (bayyinat) are required?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific legal domains where formal evidentiary proofs (bayyinat) are strictly required, emphasizing lineage, inheritance, and fixed punishments (hudud). In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction highlights the procedural rigor applied to establishing personal status and divine limits, contrasting with areas where presumption of continuity (istishab) or other evidentiary types may suffice. The inclusion of 'hudud' underscores the evidentiary threshold necessary to implement corporal or financial penalties without doubt.
